headline: The US Treasury Secretary said rising bond yields are a worldwide trend and that AI spending is not a bubble.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a senior official on the record, same week the Bank of England warned of AI-debt risks.
importance_line: Borrowing costs for home buyers and governments are at two-decade highs and the Treasury chief says that is a global move, not a US problem, which reassures markets only if investors agree with him.
summary: Bloomberg reports, citing an interview Scott Bessent gave to Axios published on Saturday, that the US Treasury Secretary sees the rise in Treasury yields as part of a global trend rather than a US-specific alarm, and that he rejects talk of an AI bubble because Microsoft, Google and Meta are earning strong revenue on their AI spending. The 10-year yield touched its highest level since 2002 this week and mortgage rates sit above 7 percent, with energy prices from the Iran war, US fiscal worries and AI borrowing all blamed; "I can't control the bond market," Bessent said.
notes: Bloomberg blocked here; text read on Yahoo Finance copy. First reporter of the interview is Axios; Bloomberg credited.
